promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The end of the war and its impact

questions.q: Which European country ruled Vietnam as part of its colonial empire (French Indochina) before the Second World War?
questions.explain: Vietnam was governed by France as part of French Indochina until the mid-twentieth century.

questions.q: Who was the communist leader of the Vietminh who declared Vietnamese independence in 1945?
questions.explain: Ho Chi Minh led the Vietminh independence movement and proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Vietnam in 1945.

questions.q: At which 1954 battle were French forces decisively defeated, effectively ending French rule in Indochina?
questions.explain: The French surrender at Dien Bien Phu in 1954 forced them to negotiate their withdrawal from Vietnam.

questions.q: The 1954 Geneva Agreement temporarily divided Vietnam along which line of latitude?
questions.explain: Geneva split Vietnam at the 17th parallel into a communist North and an anti-communist South.

questions.q: What name was given to the communist guerrilla fighters operating within South Vietnam from 1960?
questions.explain: The Vietcong (National Liberation Front) waged a communist guerrilla campaign inside South Vietnam.

questions.q: What was the name of the 1964 naval incident used by President Johnson to justify greatly increased US military involvement?
questions.explain: Reported attacks on US ships in the Gulf of Tonkin led Congress to pass the resolution authorising escalation.

questions.q: What was the name of the sustained US aerial bombing campaign against North Vietnam that began in 1965?
questions.explain: Operation Rolling Thunder was the prolonged bombing of North Vietnam launched in 1965.

questions.q: What was the name of President Nixon's policy of withdrawing US troops while training the South Vietnamese army to take over the fighting?
questions.explain: Vietnamisation aimed to hand combat to South Vietnamese forces so US troops could be withdrawn.

questions.q: The 'domino theory' used to justify US involvement argued that:
options: if one country in a region fell to communism, neighbouring countries would soon follow
communism would collapse if one country left it
the USA should never intervene in Asian affairs
Vietnam should be reunited through free elections
questions.explain: US leaders feared that a communist Vietnam would trigger the fall of neighbouring states like a row of dominoes.

questions.q: Why did the USA support the South Vietnamese leader Ngo Dinh Diem despite his unpopularity and corruption?
options: because he promised genuine free national elections
because he was a committed democrat
because he was chosen by Ho Chi Minh
questions.explain: The USA valued Diem chiefly as an anti-communist barrier, overlooking his authoritarian and corrupt rule.

questions.q: Why were the nationwide reunification elections promised for 1956 in the Geneva Agreement never held?
options: because Diem and the USA feared the communist Ho Chi Minh would win
because North Vietnam refused to take part
because the United Nations banned them
because France insisted on keeping control
questions.explain: Diem, backed by the USA, blocked the elections because Ho Chi Minh was expected to win a united vote.

questions.q: What did the US 'search and destroy' tactic involve?
options: patrols locating and attacking Vietcong forces before withdrawing, often destroying villages
building fortified bases to defend South Vietnamese cities
negotiating local ceasefires with the Vietcong
parachuting supplies to isolated South Vietnamese units
questions.explain: Search and destroy sent patrols to find and kill Vietcong, frequently burning villages and alienating civilians.

questions.q: Why did the US military use chemicals such as Agent Orange and napalm in Vietnam?
options: to destroy the jungle cover and crops that hid and fed the Vietcong
to purify drinking water for troops
to signal the location of enemy bases
to create harmless smokescreens for retreats
questions.explain: Agent Orange defoliated jungle and crops while napalm burned vegetation and positions, aiming to deny the Vietcong cover and food.

questions.q: Why is the Tet Offensive of 1968 seen as a turning point in the war?
options: although a military setback for the communists, it convinced many Americans the war could not be won
it was a decisive military victory that captured Saigon for the Vietcong
it forced North Vietnam to surrender
it ended all US bombing of the North
questions.explain: Despite heavy communist losses, Tet's scale shattered US claims of imminent victory and boosted anti-war feeling.

questions.q: Why did the My Lai Massacre of 1968 damage support for the war in the USA?
options: it exposed US troops killing hundreds of unarmed civilians, shocking public opinion
it revealed that the USA was losing every battle
it showed the Vietcong were winning the air war
it proved the domino theory was correct
questions.explain: News of US soldiers massacring unarmed villagers at My Lai outraged the public and fuelled the anti-war movement.

questions.q: What was the outcome for South Vietnam after the 1973 Paris Peace Accords led to full US withdrawal?
options: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon in 1975, reuniting Vietnam under communism
South Vietnam survived as an independent capitalist state
the country was permanently divided at the 17th parallel
the USA re-invaded to defend Saigon
questions.explain: Once US forces left, the North overran the South and took Saigon in 1975, uniting Vietnam under communist rule.

questions.q: A US soldier reports that he cannot tell Vietcong fighters apart from ordinary villagers, who help lay hidden traps. This best illustrates the difficulty of fighting:
questions.explain: Blending with civilians and using ambushes and traps were hallmarks of the Vietcong's guerrilla warfare.

questions.q: North Vietnam moved troops and supplies south through a network of paths running through neighbouring Laos and Cambodia to avoid US forces. This network was known as:
questions.explain: The Ho Chi Minh Trail through Laos and Cambodia kept the Vietcong supplied despite heavy US bombing.

questions.q: In the late 1960s American families watched largely uncensored footage of the war, including civilian casualties, on television each evening. What was the most likely effect of this?
options: growing public opposition to the war
stronger public support for escalating the war
increased trust in government war reports
questions.explain: Graphic televised images turned many Americans against the war and swelled the anti-war movement.

questions.q: A US commander reports a high enemy 'body count' but admits his troops still hold no extra territory. This best illustrates the limitations of which approach?
options: the search and destroy war of attrition strategy
questions.explain: Measuring success by body counts rather than ground gained exposed the flaws of the attrition-based search and destroy strategy.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE History (4HI1) specification; The Vietnam Conflict 1945-75
